mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the federal funds rate above 2.5% over the next month reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns in the following 20-day window.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during the previous 30-day period of lower rates (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in employment (PAYEMS) exceeding 5,000 jobs signals labor market strength that supports corporate earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant correlation with monthly PAYEMS surprise (Spearman's rho < 0.2).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in consumer demand proxies (HOUST) accompanied by a drop in industrial production (INDPRO) creates a dual contraction in economic activity, which is associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: both HOUST and INDPRO fall by > 3% in the same month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly different from a baseline of stable demand and production (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained acceleration in industrial production (INDPRO) growth above 2% per month suggests supply-side expansion that outpaces demand absorption, pushing S&P 500 forward returns negative over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positively correlated with INDPRO growth (Spearman's rho > 0.15).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate falls below 4% (UNRATE), central banks are statistically more likely to cut policy rates, lowering discount rates and boosting equity present value, which drives positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: In regimes where UNRATE < 4% but FEDFUNDS remains unchanged, 20-day forward returns show no significant improvement over prior periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in monthly pay growth (PAYEMS) of over 2% indicates wage inflation that outpaces productivity, which is associated with higher consumer spending and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher when PAYEMS growth exceeds 2% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of declining consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 0.5% suggest the Federal Reserve is less likely to raise rates, stabilizing discount rates and supporting equity valuations, which predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL remains below 0.5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not higher than during the prior month when CPIAUCSL was above 0.5% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in the industrial production index (INDPRO) followed by a sustained decline in consumer demand (HOUST) creates a dual contraction that reduces economic momentum, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by > 5% in a month and HOUST falls by > 2% in the following month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly different from a baseline of stable production and demand (t-test p > 0.05).
